This course takes you from zero, with no programming, terminal or Git experience assumed, to designing, building, deploying and operating a real backend system. You learn by building one project that grows with every lesson.

[Start with lesson 0.1 →](part-0-start-here/01-what-is-a-backend.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}

## What you will build

**Atlas** answers questions about a real open-source codebase, [PyTorch-Ignite](https://github.com/pytorch/ignite), and cites the exact file and line behind every claim.

**Atlas Agents** watches that project for new "good first issue" tickets and prepares an **Issue Brief** for each one: a plain summary, the relevant code, the project's conventions, the commands to run the tests, and a reproduction script it has verified actually fails. You then write the fix yourself. Atlas never posts to GitHub and never writes your code.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  You -->|ask a question| Atlas
  Atlas -->|answer with file:line citations| You
  GitHub[New good first issue] --> Agents[Atlas Agents]
  Agents -->|Issue Brief + verified reproduction| You
  You -->|you write the fix| PR[Your pull request]
```

## How every lesson works

1. **Analogy** for intuition.
2. **Theory**, explained precisely.
3. **Diagrams** where a picture says it better.
4. **Project code** for this step, with comments that explain *why*.
5. **Common mistakes**.
6. **Quiz**, with explanations.
7. **Exercise**, guided, with a hidden solution.
8. **Stretch** challenge, with a hidden solution.

Each part ends with a **review and practice** lesson: tasks without step-by-step help, because following along is not the same as building alone.

## The code

Everything lives in the [course repository](https://github.com/ashu-tagore/Learning_FastAPI). You write your own code in your own repository, `my-atlas`; the reference implementation is in `atlas/`, tagged at the end of each part so you can compare.
